units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Mr Tobin and Mr Hollis, I have read all of it twice with my glasses on. I do not count. I listen. They follow me from 8 to 6 and stop when I stop, and I do not need them to be anything else. Please do not touch the cupboard, Mr Tobin. In 1987 a man from the council touched it and we had no stair lights for a month. Please do not argue on my account. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Forty-three steps. Thirty-eight steps. Now a grown man proposes switching off the fire escape lights on purpose at half past one in the morning to see what happens. If anybody touches that cupboard I will report it to Kerrow and to the fire brigade, in that order. On the third floor we use the stairs like adults and count nothing. This is hysteria from the upper floors.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: For clarity, since it's being said on my behalf: I haven't said anyone is lying. I've said the extra steps need a source, and that the test as proposed can't tell a source from the building. Tobin, I'd also ask you not to isolate a fire escape circuit. If someone falls in the dark during your test, the result won't matter to anybody.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: 1. I have not touched the cupboard. 2. I proposed it, and I accept the objection. 3. Hollis: 'the building' is not a source. Each time an explanation is tested you supply another. A second stair core. A neighbour. Plant. A treadmill, probably, next week. At some point the null hypothesis has to be allowed to fail, or it is not a hypothesis, it is a preference.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: And at some point the alternative has to say what it predicts. 'Not echoes' isn't a hypothesis either. Mine predict a source somewhere in the structure, and I've told you how to look for it. Yours predicts only that I'm wrong. I'm genuinely happy to be wrong. Tell me what you'd expect to hear if it's something else, and we'll test that instead.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I read all of this after shift in my van. I am tired of it. From tonight I use the lift, when the lift works, which is not tonight because of wind. Not because of anything. Because I am tired after twelve hours. Tobin, you keep my file. Hollis, you are polite, but you were not on the stairs. That is all from me.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: this thread has gone from steps to philosophy. tobin, hollis, i love you both, but you're arguing about whether you're allowed to be wrong while the building is literally swaying in a gale. benedikt, welcome to lift squad. lift squad currently has no lift

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Jordie: the building is not 'literally swaying', it deflects a few millimetres at the top in gusts, by design. Wendell: a proposal is not an offence, and the fire brigade will laugh at you. Irena: I apologise. I will not touch it. Benedikt: understood, and thank you for the file.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (14.) For what it's worth, Tobin, if you lie very still on the floor up here during a gust you can feel it lean, which I did, for research. A few millimetres feels like more at the top. Can we stop now? The wind is doing all the footsteps tonight anyway, and it's doing them very loudly.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Locking this thread. Three pages of neighbours telling each other what they're allowed to think, a proposal to switch off fire escape lighting, and Benedikt has given up the stairs because of how this made him feel, which tells me what I need to know. Tobin's walk results stay up for anyone who wants them. There'll be a new thread when Kerrow actually fix the relay. The storm is here: knock on a neighbour instead. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Soraya, Mrs Okafor, who lived in 4A before the new family, moved to Tollinby through the council list. She told me the housing officer who helped her was a Mr Peake, on the second floor of the civic offices, who is kind but prefers letters to telephone calls. Write to him, by hand if you can, and mention the children first. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: love go in person if you can when the storm's done, they've got a ticket machine like at the deli counter and if you sit there long enough with a toddler on your knee somebody comes out and sees you, that's how my sister got her move, she took a flask and a colouring book and waited it out

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Torches on strings in a fire escape. Somebody will catch a sleeve on one in the dark, go down a flight, and Kerrow will blame the association. I am only saying what everyone else is thinking and is too polite to write.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Wendell, they're tied to the landing rails, not hung across the stairs. I went and looked at all three this afternoon in my coat. They stay until the relay is fixed. If anyone catches a sleeve on one, you may say you told us so. Bev, DCRA

units.title: Storm: shop hours, the lift, and checking on people
units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Shop opens at 06:00 as normal and stays open until the power goes or I do. Torches, batteries, tealights and matches at cost price. Bottled water, two packs per flat so everybody gets some. If you can't get down, ring the shop and Jordie or I will bring it up. Please don't go out on the balconies in this. H

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: love I've just walked home from the depot sideways, the wind on Quay Road took my hat and a man's umbrella went past me inside out like a bat, they've pulled all the double deckers into the wash bay so tonight I'll be mopping round them like a hen round her eggs, Hassan put me down for tealights please

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Lift switched itself off at 09:05. So the lift does know when it is windy, and the student was right. I take back what I said about the lift. I do not take back what I said about the bins, which are now in the car park and, in one case, on the roof of the bus shelter.

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Notice ref KE/DC/1114. The passenger lift at Dellow Court has been taken out of service as a precaution during high winds, in accordance with the manufacturer's guidance. It will be returned to service when wind speeds permit. Residents requiring assistance should contact the out-of-hours line. Kerrow Estates thanks residents for their patience.

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: the roof door is banging like mad, you can hear it from 12. mum says its the wind but its banging in a pattern?? like 3 bangs then stop then 3 bangs. is anyone going to check it. I could check it, I have a torch from Hassan

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Kids finally down. Little M. has decided the wind is the building snoring and I'm not correcting him. Carried R. up eleven floors after his granny dropped them back, with the lift off, and I'm now a different shape. Thank you to whoever left a row of tealights in jam jars on the 11 landing. That was kind.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: The jam jars were Irena, she asked me for the tealights and did every landing from 6 to 12 herself before lunch. Sold out of tealights by four. Jordie carried water up to 9, 10 and 12 this afternoon, eighteen litres a trip, legend. More stock tomorrow if the van gets down Quay Road. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: carried 54 litres up the stairs today and nothing followed me except my own regrets. daytime stairs are just stairs. ollie, do not check the roof door. the roof door is not your job and the roof is not a place, in a storm, for anyone, including me

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: The residents' meeting is postponed to next week, as half of us can't get down the stairs. Thank you, Hassan, Jordie and Irena. Please knock on your neighbours tonight, especially anyone on their own on 4, 7 and 13. If you hear glass, ring the out-of-hours line and then ring me. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (14, a report from the top.) Ollie is right that it bangs in threes. It's the wind: the door's catch is loose and the gusts come in sets. I've wedged a folded cereal box in it (the badger client's samples, finally useful) and now it only rattles. I am not going out onto a roof in a storm to see who's knocking. The answer is the storm.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Gladly, young man. Don't play them on any machine that hasn't been cleaned, and don't fast-wind them; let them rest a day in the warm first so the layers settle. Bring them to Tollinby after the storm, or post them in a padded envelope with a note of anything written on the cards. I'll put the kettle on. Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: On call tonight; the hospital generator has been tested twice already, which is either reassuring or not. Gerald is safe in his foam box under my desk. If the Met's lull comes tomorrow night I'll drive up to tern's and we can at least set levels together. Headphones on, storm off.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Woods are shut. Three trees across the reservoir road by the lay-by and one on the pumping house fence. Overflow channel's running and the dam path is under water at the bottom. The estate's not paying me to dig recordists out from under a fourth tree, so stay home, the lot of you.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Gilliver: the harbour wall gauge read 51 knots at 21:00. Hydrophones stayed home in the shed. The harbour doesn't need a microphone tonight; you could hear it from the chippy with the door shut.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Understood, Mr Ashcombe. Nobody's going anywhere tonight. For the group: no recording until the road is clear and the paths are walked. I'll post here when we have a night. Tern, did you get a chance to look at the 23:53 file from the test?

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I looked. I'm not posting it yet. there's something between the two hits that I want to hear on proper headphones before anyone else does, because if I post it now everyone will hear what I tell them to hear. it's probably the sheep. raw and slowed together when I've slept on it, promise

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Thank you, tern, for not posting a half-listened file with a caption. That is exactly the habit we want, and it's rarer than it should be. Take the time, post the raw alongside anything processed, and don't title it.

units.title: Brackwater knocks remastered (headphones on, trust me)
units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys I took the knock files from dunlin's old thread and tern's pumping house one, cleaned them up, added reverb and a drone underneath so you can actually feel it, and uploaded to my channel, link in bio. this is genuinely the scariest thing I've ever heard and I've been to the Dellow stairwell (the outside of it). insane

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: I'd rather you took it down. Those files were shared here for analysis. Adding reverb and a drone removes exactly the information we're trying to look at: the attack, the decay, the room. Make of it what you will, but please take it down, here and on your channel.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: also you put music over my pumping house file and that's my sheep. you can't remix my sheep. ok that sounds stupid but you know what I mean

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Removed. NightScreamLive, this is a formal warning. Rule 4: don't repost other members' recordings without permission, and never with added processing presented as the original. You've been asked by both recordists to take them down from your channel too. Please do.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: For anyone who heard the remix before it came down: the 'growl' under the third knock is a pitch-shifted copy of the drone he added. It isn't in the source files. I checked against the originals in the shared folder. Please don't quote it.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: ok ok it's gone from here. still on the channel though, it's called content, look it up. 400 views in two hours, more than this whole forum gets in a month

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Please don't touch anything Gerald records when we do the session. I'll watermark every file if I have to, and I'd hate to, because watermarks are ugly and Gerald has very good ears.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: One small correction to my own posts, before anyone else makes it. The article says the consultation drew 'a handful of comments'. The portal shows five: three about noise, one about boat traffic at the Gilliver slip, one in support. Five is a handful. I mention it only because someone on this board will have counted.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran

edit.text: I used to cut for Grieve. Grieve did one like this up north, the Corran job, and nobody talks about it. I was on it. I won't go into it. I just think the people on the Holm should know it's been done before, and that's all I'm saying.

units.text: I used to cut for Grieve. Grieve did one like this up north, the Corran job, and nobody talks about it. An island, like this one but smaller, eight of us, four weeks, out past the Corran Head light. I was on it. I won't go into it. I just think the people on the Holm should know it's been done before, and that's all I'm saying.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: What happened at Corran? You can't post that and walk away. There are people living on that island right now. If something went wrong on the last one, they have a right to know, and so do we. I'll put it in tonight's mailing list unless you tell me not to.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: Don't put it in anything. I said I won't go into it and I meant it. It was years ago. Maybe I shouldn't have posted. I'm leaving it up because the lads out there should know somebody's done it before them, that's all. Nothing more to it.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Corran... I've heard that name before. I'm not saying where. Some of us have been watching this company for a long time, and the pattern is there if you look at the edges, not the middle.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Hollow, you'd never heard of it before tonight and everyone reading knows it. Leave the man alone. He said what he wanted to say and asked for nothing. That's the most honest post this thread has had.

units.title: Ardent Vale's 'community update', summarised for reference.
units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Ardent Vale sent a 'community update' to its mailing list today; several of you have forwarded it to me. Summary: one reference to stewardship, two to a long-term vision, one to respect, and none to a use, a date or a number. It says the works are 'in full accordance with all consents', which is true and not in dispute. It does not answer any of the Courier's three questions.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: A whole email that says nothing. That isn't PR, it's a smokescreen. Why would a company with nothing to hide pay people to write paragraphs with no information in them? Just asking.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: companies say nothing all the time Gil. my dealership's newsletter says nothing every month, four paragraphs about 'our family values', and we're not building a bunker

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Who said bunker? I never said bunker, not once, scroll up and check. Interesting that you did, Cal. Very interesting.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: I got it too, and I have never signed up for anything from them in my life. How did they get my email address? It went straight into the same folder as the lottery wins and the cheap watches, which seems about right.

units.title: Day 14 readings: storm, day one
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 06:30, Carrow Point: 979.6 hPa and falling. Wind SSW 38 knots, gust 54 at 05:40. Air 12.0 C. Rain 14.2 mm since midnight. Visibility under 1 km in rain and spray, the light's a smudge from my kitchen. The Met's amber started at 06:00 and for once I agree with every word of it.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: My barometer at home fell 22 hPa in 24 hours. Strictly that meets the textbook definition of a 'weather bomb', which I mention only because the radio has started saying it and someone will ask whether it's a real term. It is. It's still only weather, though it's a lot of it.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 15:20: lost a cup off the anemometer to a gust I didn't get to measure, which is the most annoying sentence a man with a weather station can write. Readings from now are from the spare on the shed roof, which reads a touch low. Pressure 975.1 hPa and still going.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00: 973.8 hPa. Gust 56 knots on the spare at 19:40. The low centre should pass to the north of us before midnight and that's when the strongest gusts will come round on the back of it. Gilliver had the sea over the wall on the evening tide, according to my sister-in-law, who was not supposed to be out looking.

units.title: Storm, day one: roads, damage and help.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A single thread for the duration, so the General board stays readable. Blocked roads, damage, and offers of help go here, with roughly where you are. Please don't photograph other people's damaged houses or cars without asking them. If you need emergency help, ring for it first and post afterwards. Stay in if you can. Pell (Admin).

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Lisle: every ferry off, as predicted by me, the app and the man with the barometer. The office has said 'work from home if you can safely do so'. My manager, who lives above the office, emailed at 07:01 to say he was in. The rest of Lisle is in its kitchens watching the pier lights go in and out of the spray.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Weyhaven: the bus shelter on Quay Road has gone. Not damaged. Gone. The frame is there and the roof and both side panels are not. I drove that route for thirty-one years and I never saw that shelter so much as lose a timetable.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby: school closed, all three home. We've built a fort out of the sofa cushions and they're charging me admission, payable in biscuits. Lights flickered twice at lunch and then went off at half one, so it's candles and the gas hob. Freezer is shut and taped and nobody is allowed to look at it.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Gilliver: the electric flickered three times after dinner and stayed on, which my nephew says is the Gilliver line being stubborn as usual. I have lit the lamp in the front window anyway, and the one on the stairs. The harbour is white all over. I cant see the Holm at all this afternoon, only spray where it ought to be.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Tollinby rd shut at the garden centre dip, flooded, a hatchback in it up to the door handles and the driver sat on the roof eating crisps till the fire crew walked him out (he's fine). Brackwater jct: the temporary lights have blown over into the hedge. Honestly the best they've worked all month.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Port ammet: two call-outs already, a sycamore on a car on Chandlers Row and a big limb through a greenhouse in Tanner Street. Not cutting anything in this wind, that's how people get hurt, but I'll be out first light tomorrow. Insured, sensible rates, I'll do pensioners first.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Brackwater: the reservoir road is shut by three trees at the lay-by, and the ridge road has a beech across it by Holly Lane. Don't drive round the barriers. The verges are soft with all this rain and you'll be in the ditch, and I'll be the one pulling you out.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Gilliver: boats all held. Two punts filled on the inner moorings, both pumped out by dark. Nothing went out to the Holm today, nothing could. Sea was over the wall on the evening tide by the lifeboat house and threw stones up on the harbour road.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Pebble has been under my duvet since the first gust and will not discuss it. I've moved all the shop buckets into the hall. If anyone on Tanner Street has lost a green wheelie bin with a number 9 on it, it's in our yard, upright, looking pleased with itself.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: fine. it's windy. I'll give you windy. still not the storm of the century, the century's only half done

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Co-op update from the van, twelve hours in: two poles down on the Brackwater ridge, an ash through the line by the reservoir, and a lot of Tollinby hanging off one feeder. Garvey says it's 'a proper one'. I say I can't feel my hands. We're doing the pumping station and the care home on Station Road first, then the most houses per job.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Thank you Tess, genuinely. The care home on Station Road has my mum's friend in it, so you've just made an old lady very happy. We'll wait. The kids have decided candles are the best thing that ever happened and want them every night forever.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Collections suspended, as announced. Week four of the recycling, then, and now a gale on top of it. I have weighted my box with a paving slab from the yard and wedged the lid with a broom handle. If it is found in Lisle, it has my house number on it in paint. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Catalogued, with thanks: MSHS/ED/1991/4. I have kept the children's spelling exactly as written, including 'hering' with one r throughout, and Ewan's grandfather's herring prices, which are in fact the most complete price series for 1930s Gilliver that the Society holds. Persistence is rewarded after all.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Kerris, a question kindly meant, and I'll accept 'no' as an answer. Have you a fixed reference for 'too tall to be a kid'? The rail, a bollard, the lamp standard? Not doubting you. It's the one detail that would settle half the arguments other people keep having on your behalf.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine room view, since I was below and saw nothing: I believe the crew saw what they say they saw. I also believe it was a person. Those two beliefs have never been in a fight, whatever the Sound Board thinks.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Fair question. The lamp standard at the top of the slip is four metres and it was nowhere near that. The handrail comes to my waist and it was well above the rail, head and shoulders, standing where the slip goes under. Dark coat, no light. That's what I had on the fifth and it's what I've got now.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I'm on pier duty with no ferries to meet, sat in the hut with a flask watching the Lisle slip through the window. There's nothing on it tonight but spray... ha, anyway, nobody would stand out there in this. Not even an angler. Especially not an angler.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: well above the rail. so a big lad. that narrows it down to every fisherman in gilliver and the chippy delivery driver. who is off tonight btw, no ferry no chips

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Up at four out of habit. Not going anywhere. Spray coming over the wall by the lifeboat house already and it's two hours to high water. Wind's gone round south-west like they said. I've put an extra line on the Annie and I'll not go near her again till it's done.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: chandlery open seven till twelve then I'm going home, the pontoon is moving like a dance floor. HM has closed the harbour. nobody go aboard anything in this, I mean it lads, I've got all your mothers' numbers and I'm not afraid to use them

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour Notice 14/1. Gilliver harbour is closed to all vessel movements until further notice. Owners are asked not to attempt to board vessels on moorings or pontoons during the storm. The slipway remains closed. Please report any vessel adrift to the harbour office or the Coastguard. Thank you all. HM Quill

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: The boat's in the lee berth at Port Ammet with every line we own on her. I've been aboard twice to check the gensets and bilges, which I'm allowed to do because I'm paid to and the Ammet harbourmaster said so. She's riding fine, groaning a bit on the fenders. So am I.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Kerris is right. It's shore standby, at the standby rate. And Finn, if you'd like the contract read to you, I'll do it over tea when we're running again, with the biscuits. All crossings off today and tonight. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Seth, I went down at two to check our lines from the shore side. She's fine. I'm soaked through two coats. There's a council litter bin floating upright in the Ammet harbour, bobbing along by the fish quay like it's waiting for the ferry.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: somebody's punt, the blue one with the bent outboard bracket, broke off the inner mooring and went off down the harbour on her own like she had an appointment. HM and two of the lifeboat lads got her in against the slip with a boat hook. nobody went aboard. small victories

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Brackwater ridge, 21:40. Sitting in the van waiting for the gusts to drop under the limit so we're allowed up the pole. Garvey is asleep sitting bolt upright with his flask still in his hand. I didn't know people could do that. I've been told that's what twenty-five years does to you.

units.title: Storm faults: what we're doing and why it takes as long as it does
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Plain words for anyone asking why their lights are still off. A tree through a line isn't a switch, it's a job. Make it safe, cut the tree off it, check the pole, re-string, test, switch on. Four of us, two hours if it's easy, and none of it in a gust over the limit. Forty jobs open. Hospitals and pumping stations first, then most houses per job. Your street will come. Flaming storms.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Orla wins the biscuit. IT traced it: a meter-reading autodialler at a pumping station up the coast, stuck on our number because somebody typed it into the fault-callback field years ago. It rings, waits 41 seconds for a tone that never comes, gives up, and tries again the next night at the same minute. I feel cheated and relieved in equal measure. (Queue's lit up again, back in a sec.)

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: A machine with a 41-second timeout is the most honest caller you'll ever have: it never pretends, it never wants anything, and it always hangs up on time. I'm glad it's found. I'm also a little sorry for it, which I recognise is not a clinical position.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: I'll take my biscuit in shortbread form, posted to Sound FM, care of the overnight desk, which is currently running on a generator and smells of a pasty. Glad it's a machine, Hana. I'd have told you it was, but it's nicer when IT says it.

units.title: The 03:10 buzzer: a damp junction box
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: The electrician came this afternoon. The junction box for the front door intercom sits behind the porch gutter, which overflows, and it was full of water: green on the terminals, a little puddle in the bottom. He dried it, replaced it and sealed it. He says a damp contact can chatter at the same temperature every night, which would be why 03:10. Mrs A. asked me tonight if her caller had been. I said not tonight. She said 'he'll come another way, then', and went back to sleep.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Ours was a stuck call button, yours is a wet box. I'm starting to think every intercom in the world is quietly falling apart and we only notice at three in the morning because it's the only time anyone listens to them. Give Mrs A. my best. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: The temperature explanation is a good one. Contacts open and close as the metal contracts in the cold, and if the night cools the same way each night, it trips at the same minute. It's lovely to see a mechanism this tidy. Mrs A.'s reply is not something I can explain, and I don't think it needs explaining.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Liv's Mrs A. said that to me too, once, when I came to collect Liv off a late. 'He'll come another way.' Old folk say things. She also told me my boots were too loud for a corridor, which was fair. Home on the bus.

units.title: Retail park in the storm: a report from Control's least favourite guard
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Trolley bays chained by two, as instructed. At 23:40 a gust took the whole plastic roof off the bay by the pet shop and carried it the length of the car park, end over end, like a playing card. Nobody hurt, no cars hit. I'd write 'patrolled, nil found' but it was very much found. It's in the hedge by the drive-through.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: No lifts here either tonight, our wind limit's 20 m/s and Halvard's gusting past that even this far inland. Thinking of you Weyhaven lot. I'm in the site cabin watching the jib weathervane round on its slew brake, which is the most relaxing thing a crane ever does. It's like watching a very tall cat turn round before lying down.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Yard floodlights went at 01:50, all at once. Generator took forty seconds to kick in, and the whole night shift stood at the dock doors in the dark watching the trailers rock on their legs. Nobody said a word for forty seconds. Then the lights came back and my scanner said 'too slow'.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: A&E 'blown over' count tonight: nine. Two wrists, a lot of knees, and one man who went out at midnight to hold his greenhouse door shut and lost the argument. Everyone fine, in the end. The vending machine on B is still keeping our money. Some things a storm can't change.

units.title: Listening to the overnight show by candlelight
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Power's off in Tollinby, so I'm in the shop with the radio on batteries and a candle in a saucer, reading by it like a clerk in an old novel. The overnight show is taking storm calls: a woman in Lisle whose greenhouse has gone over the wall, a man whose chimney pot is, in his words, 'in the bath'. Orla, if you read this, your voice is the warmest thing in the building.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Thank you. I'm in a studio on generator power eating a cold pasty. The greenhouse woman rang back at half three to say she'd found her tomato plants in the next garden, still in their pots. That was the lead item. It's been that kind of night.

units.title: Storms are convenient
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Funny how a storm arrives just as a certain island gets into the papers. Roads shut, ferries off, nobody looking... watch what gets moved while nobody's watching. I'm not saying what. People who've been paying attention will know.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Three questions, and they're not rhetorical: what, specifically, is being moved, by whom, and to where? If you can't answer any of the three, it isn't a pattern. It's a low-pressure system crossing a coast, which they do every autumn, papers or no papers.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: The van man waved! And bought a loaf, and two rolls for later. He says the agency is moving him onto days from next month, so he won't be outside any more. Is it strange that I'll miss a man I've spoken to twice, through a van window, about cinnamon?

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Not strange. Regulars are regulars. There's a grey cat that sits on the port road gatepost every night at two and I log it. If it stopped coming, I'd notice. Logged: van man, days, missed.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Different weather out here from all you coast folks: dry as a bone and bitter, minus fourteen with the wind on the scales at the elevator junction. Coffee froze a skin in the cup holder in the time it took me to check the tyres. Hearing about your storm on the CB from a driver who came up from the coast. Stay in, all of you.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: I ate a vegetable (it was inside a sandwich, it still counts). the new sensor is so boring. it only comes on when I walk past it. I didn't realise how much company the broken one was. back to the lab, chapter 3 now has a title and an introduction and a lot of empty space
